summary: Radiofrequency energy used to support skin-firmness and texture concerns.
leadAnswer: Radiofrequency (RF) treatments use controlled energy, delivered from the skin surface with no needles, to warm the deeper layers of the skin. Kaiteki runs four RF platforms, and a doctor examines your skin before choosing one.
seoTitle: Radiofrequency Treatment Malaysia | Skin Firmness | Kaiteki
seoDescription: Radiofrequency (RF) treatment in Malaysia to support skin firmness and texture concerns. Book a free consultation with a Kaiteki doctor to assess suitability.

routes.title: Skin firmness across the lower face
routes.body: Heats the dermis to prompt collagen change across a broader area than a focused device.

routes.title: Laxity in the lower lid
routes.body: Gentle heating to prompt collagen change where the lower lid skin has loosened and creased. Considered where crepiness accompanies the darkness rather than where a hollow dominates.

variantModule.heading: BTL Exilis, Oligio X, Wonderface or XERF: which RF platform, and why
variantModule.intro: The four platforms differ in how deep the energy reaches and how the surface is cooled.

items.title: BTL Exilis
items.body: Monopolar delivery with embedded surface cooling lets the device keep working at a depth that reaches subcutaneous fat, which is why it is used for body-contour concerns as well as facial firmness.

items.title: Oligio X
items.body: A Korean monopolar platform delivered shot by shot through a cooled tip that monitors contact, studied mainly for mild to moderate laxity of the lower face.

items.title: Wonderface
items.body: A face-specific platform pairing bipolar radiofrequency, more contained and comparatively superficial, with a separate neuromuscular stimulation mode that works on muscle tone.

items.title: XERF
items.body: Combines 6.78 MHz and 2 MHz so energy can be biased towards shallower or deeper tissue, with integrated cryogen cooling.

ctaMid.heading: Not sure whether radiofrequency or another energy fits your skin?
ctaMid.body: Surface RF, focused ultrasound and RF microneedling reach tissue differently. A doctor can tell you which your skin calls for.

avoidIf.body: such as a pacemaker, in or near the treatment area.

avoidIf.lead: Active skin infection or inflamed areas
avoidIf.body: where the treatment would be applied.

sessionSteps.title: Consultation and assessment
sessionSteps.body: The doctor assesses your skin's thickness and laxity, which decide the device and settings.

sessionSteps.title: The treatment
sessionSteps.body: Controlled RF energy is delivered to the target areas, with contact cooling for comfort. Most people describe a warm, deep, massage-like sensation that builds and eases as the handpiece moves.

sessionSteps.title: Afterwards
sessionSteps.body: Sessions in a course are usually spaced about 4 to 6 weeks apart.

bands.title: Straight afterwards
bands.body: Mild redness or a feeling of warmth may occur and typically settles within a few hours.

bands.title: The same day
bands.body: Most people return to normal activities, and makeup can generally be worn straight after a facial session.

afterSession.aftercare: Gentle skincare and daily sun protection afterwards.

risks.common: Redness, warmth or mild swelling that usually settles.
risks.pigmentNote: RF heats tissue rather than targeting pigment, so it does not rely on colour contrast and is used across a wide range of skin tones, including Asian skin.
cannotDo: It is not a substitute for surgery where there is significant excess skin.
It does not change the skin on the day; any change depends on slow tissue remodelling.
risks.disclose: Tell your doctor about anything on the avoid list above, including implanted devices anywhere near the treatment area.

costFactors.intro: Kaiteki does not quote prices online, because the course is set by what the assessment finds. What moves the cost:
factors: The area treated. Face-only plans differ from face-and-neck or body plans.
The number of sessions in the course.

relatedReasons.microneedling: Radiofrequency delivered through fine needles, used for texture and scarring, with more recovery time.
relatedReasons.hifu: Focused ultrasound for laxity at a chosen depth, a different energy type from radiofrequency.

sections.heading: What is radiofrequency (RF) treatment?
body: Radiofrequency (RF) treatment is a non-surgical approach that uses controlled energy to warm the deeper layers of the skin, rather than acting on the surface as skincare does.

sections.heading: How does radiofrequency warm the skin without needles?
body: RF devices deliver controlled thermal energy into the dermis, gently heating the tissue. This warming is intended to act on existing collagen fibres and to prompt the skin's own gradual collagen-renewal response over time.

faqs.q: Are radiofrequency treatments suitable for sensitive skin?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Surface RF is non-invasive and generally well tolerated, and settings are adjusted to your skin. Mention any retinoids or recent peels, which change what the skin will tolerate.

faqs.q: Is there any downtime after RF treatment?
faqs.a: Usually minimal. Mild redness or warmth typically settles within a few hours, and most people go straight back to normal activities.

faqs.q: How many radiofrequency sessions will I need?
faqs.a: A course of about 2 to 3 sessions is common, sometimes followed by maintenance every 6 to 12 months.
Any change develops gradually over weeks to months and varies between people.
